title.narrative: PROGRESS REPORT ON ANTI CORRUPTION COLLECTIVE

description.narrative: Ghana’s business environment has become increasingly uncertain because the macroeconomic environment is unstable and the cost of doing business is high. Ghana’s economy has suffered a significant hit by a perfect storm of global and domestic economic challenges. The attendant effects of the conflict in Ukraine (high energy and food prices) intensified the economic shocks after the pandemic, and domestic fiscal recklessness has hurt livelihoods and businesses. The local currency has depreciated by about 40 percent between 2022 and 2023, inflation is 43 percent, and the commercial lending rate is almost 40 percent. This worrying state of the economy has made it difficult for businesses to operate, hampered job creation, and threatened the sustainability of several enterprises. Even though Ghana has signed a three-year Extend Credit Facility Programme with the IMF towards economic recovery, this has also required the government to introduce additional tax handles and quarterly adjustments of energy prices, which has compounded the already high cost of doing business. These headwinds pose a severe threat to the investment climate, and negatively affect critical value chains like horticulture and other subsectors, which has already recorded a decline in export volumes. The overarching aim of the project is to advocate for an improved business environment and investment climate for foreign investors, specifically focusing on members of the Ghana-Netherland Business and Culture Council. This survey instrument is intended to collect information on the perception of members of the GNBCC and other affiliated businesses about the overall investment climate and the alternative reforms to make Ghana an investment destination. The survey instrument is organized in five (5) sections: Organizational Profile, Investment in Ghana, Cost of doing business, and Investors perception of the business environment. The information collected through this survey is solely for research purposes, and in no way can an information be traced to your organization.

The overall objective is for GNBCC to promote Ghana as a business investment destination and to monitor the attractiveness of doing business in Ghana. In the past eight years, there has been no improvement in the (foreign) investment climate, GNBCC is tracking the progress under the chapter “Enabling Environment”.

title.narrative: Reviewing Current Economic and Investment Challenges and Opportunities for Shared Benefits and Growth- a focus on the Members of the Ghana-Netherland Business and Cultural Counc

description.narrative: Through research and stakeholder engagement, this project seeks to advocate for an improved business environment and investment climate for foreign investors in Ghana, specifically focusing on members of the Ghana-Netherland Business and Culture Council. Key Objectives of the Project are: 1. Understand the investment challenges from the perspective of the members of GNBCC. 2. Identify the feasible solutions to improve the investment climate and business environment in the (horticulture) industry and its supporting value chain. 3. Increase government awareness of the challenges in the (horticulture) industry and its value chain, and the solutions to boost investment in the sector.
